sections.h2: How is Michigan organized when you sell a house?
sections.html:
Michigan has 83 counties, and nearly every record tied to a home sale lives at the county level. Property is assessed by a city or township assessor, taxes are collected by local and county treasurers, and the deed is recorded by the county register of deeds.

Four offices come up again and again:

  • The city or township assessor, who sets assessed and taxable value and takes the transfer notice after a sale.
  • The local treasurer, who collects the summer and winter bills, and the county treasurer, who takes over unpaid accounts.
  • The register of deeds, who records the deed and any mortgage release.
  • The county probate court, if the owner has died.

The county sections further down group our local pages by county, with property tax and register of deeds guides first and city pages after them. For a flat index, see Michigan guides by city and county. If your county or city is not listed, the state rules below still apply and the county office can answer local questions.

sections.h2: When are Michigan property taxes due, and what if they are unpaid at closing?
sections.html:
Michigan bills property tax twice a year, and the unpaid balance travels with the house until someone pays it. Summer taxes are billed in early July and are due by September 14. Winter taxes carry a December 1 lien date and are due February 14. Taxes still unpaid at the end of February are turned over to the county treasurer on March 1 with a 4 percent county administration fee, according to the Michigan Treasury FAQ.

Tax foreclosure moves on a fixed calendar, and it is run by the county treasurer:

  • Property that has been delinquent for 12 months or more is forfeited to the county treasurer on March 1, and a $175 fee is added (MCL 211.78g).
  • The owner can redeem by paying everything owed on or before the March 31 after the foreclosure judgment, or within 21 days after judgment in a contested case.
  • After that date, title vests in the foreclosing unit.

If you are behind, a sale before the redemption deadline can pay the balance out of proceeds at closing. Ask the county treasurer for a written payoff figure. Our Michigan property tax guide and the page on tax deed and tax lien sales go through the steps in more detail. If you think the assessment is wrong, the Michigan Tax Tribunal page covers appeal deadlines.

sections.h2: What changes in your tax bill when a Michigan house is sold?
sections.html:
The buyer's taxable value usually jumps, and the buyer is the one who has to tell the assessor. Michigan caps yearly growth in taxable value at the lesser of 5 percent or the rate of inflation. When ownership transfers, the cap resets and taxable value for the following year becomes the state equalized value (MCL 211.27a). The new owner must notify the local assessor within 45 days on the State Tax Commission form. We explain the form on our property transfer affidavit page.

Sellers have a form to think about too. A principal residence is exempt from local school operating millage if the owner files an affidavit with the assessor, and the exemption ends when the home is sold or stops being the owner's main home. Owners must rescind within 90 days of that change. Details are on our principal residence exemption page.

sections.h2: What does it cost to transfer and record a deed in Michigan?
sections.html:
Michigan charges a state and a county transfer tax on most deeds, plus a flat recording fee. The table below shows the figures we confirmed in the statutes.

ItemAmountSource
State real estate transfer tax$3.75 per $500 of value or fraction of $500MCL 207.525
County real estate transfer tax$0.55 per $500 in counties under 2,000,000 people; up to $0.75 in larger countiesMCL 207.504
Recording fee at the register of deeds$30 per document, any page countMCL 600.2567
Transfer notice to the assessorDue from the buyer within 45 daysMCL 211.27a
Summer and winter tax due datesSeptember 14 and February 14Michigan Treasury

Some transfers are exempt from the state tax, such as a deed from a parent to a child. Our Michigan transfer tax page lists them, and quitclaim deeds and closing costs have their own guides. We could not confirm a statewide rule on who pays, so check your purchase agreement.

sections.h2: How does foreclosure work in Michigan?
sections.html:
Most Michigan mortgage foreclosures happen outside court. A mortgage with a power of sale can be foreclosed by advertisement after a default (MCL 600.3201). The lender publishes a notice once a week for four successive weeks in a newspaper in the county, and a copy is posted on the property within 15 days after the first publication (MCL 600.3208). The sale then takes place at the county level.

After the sale, the owner still has a right to redeem for a set time. For one to four unit residential property under a mortgage made after 1964, the statute sets:

  • 6 months when the amount claimed is more than two thirds of the original debt.
  • 1 month when the property is abandoned under the statute.
  • 1 year when neither of those applies.

The statute has more branches than we list, so an attorney or housing counselor should confirm which period fits your loan.

sections.h2: How do you sell an inherited house in Michigan?
sections.html:
The probate court in the county where the owner lived handles the estate, and the person with legal authority signs the deed. If the estate is small, the court can turn property over to the surviving spouse or the heirs without full administration. The limit is a gross estate of $50,000 or less, and for real property with debt, the debt up to $250,000 is deducted from its value (MCL 700.3982).

Heirs other than a qualifying spouse or minor children can be responsible for the decedent's unpaid debts for 63 days after the order, up to what they received. The statute adjusts dollar figures over time, so ask the probate court for the current amount. Our Michigan probate process page walks through the steps.

sections.h2: Do you have to give a disclosure statement when you sell?
sections.html:
Often yes. Michigan's Seller Disclosure Act covers sales, land contracts and lease options for property with one to four residential units. The seller completes the state's form, and if the buyer is not given a signed statement the buyer may end an otherwise binding purchase agreement (MCL 565.957). The form is not a warranty. It records what the seller knows.

Several sellers are outside the act (MCL 565.953), including:

  • Court-ordered transfers, foreclosure sales and sales by a lender that took the property back.
  • A fiduciary who never lived in the house and is selling for an estate, guardianship or trust.
  • Transfers between co-owners and to a spouse, parent, child or grandchild.

If you are unsure whether the act applies to you, ask a Michigan real estate attorney.

sections.h2: What if the house has tenants?
sections.html:
A tenancy is a legal status the new owner steps into, so deal with it before you list. In Michigan, a landlord may end a tenancy for unpaid rent with a written 7-day notice to quit. An estate at will can be ended by either side with notice covering one month or the rent interval if it is shorter. A year-to-year tenancy needs a notice to quit as well (MCL 554.134). A tenant who stays is removed through summary proceedings in district court.

Our pages on the eviction process and landlord and tenant law give the full picture. We could not confirm whether a sale ends a lease, so read yours before you promise a buyer an empty house.

sections.h2: What does an as-is cash sale mean here?
sections.html:
It means the buyer takes the house in its current condition and you do not make repairs or hold showings. The buyer pays with cash and does not wait on a lender's appraisal, so title work and payoff letters set the pace. As-is does not cancel the Seller Disclosure Act, where it applies, and it does not hide a title problem or an unpaid tax bill from the title company.

Michigan law does not require an attorney to supervise a home closing, according to the State Bar of Michigan's journal. Title companies commonly run closings, and a seller may bring an attorney anyway. Our land contract page covers sales on contract.

sections.h2: What property issues come up with Michigan homes?
sections.html:
Radon is the one the state talks about most. Michigan's environment department says the EPA action level is 4.0 picocuries per liter, that about one in four Michigan homes tests above it, and that in some counties as many as half may. The only way to know is a test by a certified tester, and the state says radon can be reduced before or after a purchase, with funds escrowed at closing if needed.

For septic, well or flood zone questions, ask your county health department or township office, since we have not confirmed a statewide rule.

faqs.q: How many counties does Michigan have?
faqs.a: Michigan has 83 counties. Property tax collection, deed recording and probate all run through county offices, so start with the county where the house sits.

faqs.q: When are Michigan property taxes due?
faqs.a: Summer taxes are due by September 14 and winter taxes by February 14. Unpaid balances go to the county treasurer on March 1, and a 4 percent fee is added.

faqs.q: How much is the Michigan transfer tax?
faqs.a: The state tax is $3.75 per $500 of value, and the county tax is $0.55 per $500 in counties under 2,000,000 people. Some transfers are exempt, so ask the register of deeds.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house that is in foreclosure?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the sale closes before your redemption period ends. The length of that period depends on your loan, so confirm it with an attorney or a housing counselor.

faqs.q: Do I need probate to sell an inherited house?
faqs.a: Usually the probate court is involved. A small estate of $50,000 or less may be turned over without full administration, and the county probate court can tell you which path fits.

faqs.q: Do I have to fill out a seller disclosure in Michigan?
faqs.a: For most sales of one to four unit homes, yes. Court-ordered sales, many estate sales and transfers to close family are outside the act.

faqs.q: Can I sell with tenants living in the house?
faqs.a: Yes. The tenancy does not disappear on its own, so review the lease and the notice rules before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: Do you buy houses in every Michigan county?
faqs.a: We buy houses across the state. Use the county list on this page to find your local guides, or send us your address for a cash offer.
